newsitem.title: USA: Nabisco Holdings jump after restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Nabisco Holdings jump after restructuring.

text.p: Nabisco Holdings Corp. said its profits surged 21 percent in the first quarter as its restructuring last year led to efficiencies and lower operating costs.

Nabisco, the maker of products ranging from Oreo cookies to Grey Poupon mustard, said its net income surged to $64 million, or 24 cents a share, in the quarter from $53 million, or 20 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Earnings per share were slightly higher than Wall Street expectations.
Operating income rose to $196 million from $181 million.
The company said its revenues slid to $1.91 billion from 1.99 billion, as this year's quarter had three fewer domestic selling days than in the 1996 period.
Nabisco, which is 80.5 percent owned by food and tobacco giant RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp., said there was also a transitional disruption in sales as it reorganized its U.S. biscuit sales force.

"Our bottom line performance for the quarter met our expectations and clearly shows the importance of our 1996 restructuring, which has focused our efforts, increased our productivity and already has started to improve our margins," said Nabisco Chairman H. John Greeniaus.

Nabisco also said it benefited from a reduced effective income tax rate of 40.2 percent in the quarter, down from 41.1 percent in 1996. The company said it expects to maintain the tax rate for the year.
This quarter marks the first time that Parsippany, N.J.-based Nabisco is separately reporting the results of its two domestic operating groups -- U.S. Biscuit and U.S. Foods.

The U.S. Foods group, with sales in 1996 of $2.64 billion, was formed last year and manages a wide range of product lines, including the company's condiments and tablespreads businesses, nuts and canister snacks, confections and gum, pet snacks, and Nabisco's food service operations.

"By providing separate performance information for U.S. Biscuit and U.S. Foods, we will make it easier for investors both to follow these businesses and to appreciate the importance of each to Nabisco's future," Greeniaus said.

U.S. Biscuit operating profits grew 7 percent to $134 million for the quarter from $125 million. Biscuit sales dropped 8 percent to $801 million from $871 million in 1996, reflecting Nabisco's sales force reorganization and fewer selling days in the quarter vs. last year, it said.

Product highlights included the continued outstanding performance of Oreo cookies, whose sales surged 23 percent behind strong marketing as part of an overall strategy of increased emphasis on Nabisco's core brands.
Partially offsetting these gains were declines for the quarter of Newtons and SnackWells, which continue to face stiff competition from a proliferation of similar "healthful" cookies.

Nabisco's U.S. Foods Group increased operating income to $65 million from $63 million. Sales fell 6 percent to $527 million from $563 million as the company embarked on a programme to reduce high retail trade inventories of condiments and tablespreads, Nabisco said.

Planters, now the only nationally-branded nut line, continued the strong improvement begun in 1996, with sales up 7 percent and operating income up significantly. Sales rose on the growth in warehouse club stores and mass merchandising channels as well as in conventional supermarkets.

International operating income rose 8 percent to $54 million from $50 million, after several acquisitions during the second half of last year and as operating efficiencies improved in several markets, it said.
Nabisco's stock fell $2 to $38.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
